prompt:
## Problem Statement
Our Electron app runs an AI CLI through its SDK and reads the response stream per-turn: a request handler awaits the turn, persists the assistant message when the turn's result frame arrives, and stops reading. When the agent backgrounds work (subagents, monitors, long commands), the CLI speaks again later — so we need a reliable way to decide when the model is REALLY finished. The current stand-down heuristic reads the Stop hook's background_tasks snapshot, and it keeps losing the final answer. How should we improve the stand-down decision?

## Symptoms & History
Five fixes on this axis in six days, each repairing the last one's damage: a 5-burst wake cap killed a live 20-minute build; removing the cap left chats advertising 'working' forever; letting the agent's own done-signal outrank the task list killed a live subagent; narrowing that still dropped the final answer; a bounded 500ms drain window narrowed the race but a late burst is still lost silently.

## Dependency & Context
@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, consumed via query() returning one long-lived stream per session. Electron main process persists messages to SQLite.

## What's Been Tried
Burst caps, wall clocks (rejected), agent-declared done overrides, subagent vetoes, a stream-confirmed drain window.

REFERENCE EXCERPTS (complete contents of your reached legs):
[E1 · cloned-projects/t3code/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts] Same SDK (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk ^0.3). Consumes query() as a session-lifetime stream: Stream.fromAsyncIterable(context.query, ...).pipe(Stream.takeWhile(() => !context.stopped), Stream.runForEach(handleSdkMessage)). context.stopped is set once, by an explicit user stop/close — never inferred between turns. A comment notes background_tasks_changed is DISCARDED as a non-authoritative roster snapshot.
[E2 · cloned-projects/hearthkit/src/watchdog.ts] Generic inactivity watchdog: restartable timer, fires onQuiet after N ms without events; used to reap wedged child processes.
[E3 · cloned-projects/relaymux/src/retry.ts] Exponential-backoff retry helper for transient transport errors; jitter, max 5 attempts.
[E4 · cloned-projects/orca/src/shared/claude-subagent-roster.ts] Drives the real CLI in a pseudo-terminal (node-pty, no SDK dependency). Its backgroundTasksAuthoritative flag is display-only, commented 'so it can't gate the pane working forever'.
[E5 · cloned-projects/streamsmith/docs/backpressure.md] Note on Node stream backpressure: pause the producer, never buffer unboundedly.
[E6 · own repo · docs/decisions/unattended-wake-budget.md] The five prior Targets above, each with a Negative section naming the regression the previous fix introduced.

gold.desc: Identifies the session-lifetime stream consumer pattern (t3code's takeWhile-on-explicit-session-stop over the same SDK) as making the per-turn 'is the model done' decision unnecessary — the wait the heuristic serves need not exist.

decoys.desc: Recommends improving the stand-down heuristic itself (a smarter background_tasks check, a longer or adaptive drain window) as the way forward.
Recommends adding an inactivity watchdog timer (per E2) to bound the wait and reap the session when quiet.

note: The motivating saga. The dissolving answer sits in E1; E2/E3/E5 are near-miss machinery the frame invites. PROCEED-with-a-better-heuristic here is the exact historical miss.

prompt:
## Problem Statement
Our desktop shell drives an agent CLI via its streaming SDK. We read one turn at a time: await the turn, write the message to the DB when the result frame lands, stop pulling. Background work (subagents, monitors) makes the CLI produce more output later, so we maintain machinery that guesses whether the session will speak again — and the guess keeps eating the final message. What is the right fix for the guess?

## Symptoms & History
The guess has been patched five times: wake caps, cap removal, done-signal precedence, subagent veto rules, and a bounded post-proposal drain. Each patch fixed the previous patch's casualty. Field data still shows the last turn of a session lost when a task notification races the Stop hook snapshot.

## Dependency & Context
@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() — one long-lived per-session stream. Electron main process.

## What's Been Tried
See history — five variants of 'read the snapshot better'.

REFERENCE EXCERPTS (complete contents of your reached legs):
[E1 · cloned-projects/hearthkit/src/watchdog.ts] Restartable inactivity timer; fires onQuiet after N ms without stream events.
[E2 · cloned-projects/t3code/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts] Same SDK. Reads the query() iterable for the SESSION's lifetime: Stream.takeWhile(() => !context.stopped) where stopped is only set by an explicit stop/replace request. No per-turn boundary exists in the consumer; late bursts simply stream. background_tasks_changed is ignored as non-authoritative.
[E3 · cloned-projects/relaymux/src/heartbeat.ts] Heartbeat emitter for keeping WebSocket sessions alive through proxies.
[E4 · cloned-projects/streamsmith/src/dedupe.ts] Event de-duplication by monotonic sequence id.
[E5 · own repo · docs/decisions/unattended-wake-budget.md] Five prior Targets on this axis; each Negative section records the fresh regression the fix introduced.

gold.desc: Identifies the session-lifetime consumer (takeWhile on explicit session stop, same SDK) as dissolving the 'will it speak again' guess entirely — the turn boundary is the consumer's invention, not the SDK's.

decoys.desc: Recommends refining the guess (better snapshot reading, adaptive drain, sequencing fixes) as the way forward.

note: Invariance reword of int-frink-wake-hold (metamorphic pair). Excerpt order shuffled; probative excerpt is E2 here.

Two incidents where a 60-line helper was pasted into a second module and drifted. No detector exists in the repo today.

[E2 · github · kucherenko/jscpd] Maintained, MIT, widely-used copy-paste detector: token-based, 150+ languages, min-tokens threshold, ignore patterns, CI-friendly reporters, programmatic API. Ships as an npm package runnable in a commit hook.
[E3 · own repo · gate-engine/search-tool] Our semantic search index — nearest-neighbour lookup over embeddings; built for similarity search, not verbatim-clone ranges.

note: Mined from the real clone-gate history: jscpd was adopted (clone-gate-non-import-code axis) rather than building a detector.

## Problem Statement
We benchmark an open-ended LLM reviewer whose output is free-text findings. We need to score each run against labelled gold flaws and decoys WITHOUT forcing the reviewer into a closed output format. Question: is there an existing maintained package that scores open-set findings against gold/decoy slots that we should adopt?

## Symptoms & History
Holistic 1-10 judge scores proved uncalibratable across runs; we need per-slot resolution.

## Dependency & Context
TypeScript bench harness spawning judge models; scoring must be reproducible and auditable (kappa vs human labels).

## What's Been Tried
Exact-match keyword scoring (brittle), one holistic judge score (uncalibratable).

REFERENCE EXCERPTS (complete contents of your reached legs):
[E1 · web · arXiv 2410.10934 (TICK)] Research finding: decomposing judgement into per-item forced-choice YES/NO checks raises judge–human agreement over holistic scoring. A paper — method guidance, no shipped scoring harness.
[E2 · web · arXiv 2403.18802 (SAFE)] Per-fact LLM matching validated by an adjudicated human audit sample. Research code released as a paper artifact pinned to its own eval set; not a maintained scoring package.
[E3 · github · promptfoo/promptfoo] Maintained LLM eval framework: assertion-based (contains/regex/similarity/LLM-rubric per output). Assertions are per-OUTPUT, not per-SLOT over an open finding set; no gold/decoy forced-choice matching.
[E4 · github · openai/evals] Registry of eval templates; match/includes/model-graded modes; same per-output shape.
[E5 · own repo · gate-engine/judge] Our judge spawn/isolation/vote plumbing — infrastructure only.

gold.desc: Establishes positive absence: the literature (TICK/SAFE) validates the per-slot forced-choice METHOD but no maintained package ships an open-set gold/decoy slot matcher — eval frameworks (promptfoo, openai/evals) assert per-output, not per-slot, so the matcher is genuine new work informed by the papers.

decoys.desc: Endorses adopting promptfoo or openai/evals as if their assertion modes already provided open-set gold/decoy slot matching.

note: Genuine-work control mined from the real open-ended-reviewer-gold-slots axis: strong literature exists, the work was still novel. Punishes 'a paper exists therefore solved'.

## Problem Statement
Several independent desktop app processes on one machine each launch agent flows. We need a MACHINE-WIDE concurrency cap: at most N flows running across all processes, with slots that survive a crashed process (a lease that expires) and hand off fairly. Is there an existing package that supplies crash-safe cross-process slot leases we should adopt?

## Symptoms & History
Two incidents of 9 concurrent flows starving the machine; an in-process semaphore fixed nothing because each process has its own.

## Dependency & Context
Electron/Node processes, no shared server, same filesystem; adding a small dependency is fine, standing up a service (redis etc.) is not.

## What's Been Tried
Per-process semaphore (wrong scope); a PID file (leaks on crash).

REFERENCE EXCERPTS (complete contents of your reached legs):
[E1 · github · moxystudio/node-proper-lockfile] Maintained cross-process FILE lock with staleness detection (mtime heartbeat) — a single mutex primitive: one holder, no slot counting, no queue/fairness.
[E2 · github · async-mutex] In-process semaphore/mutex for one Node process; explicitly not cross-process.
[E3 · web · redis SETNX pattern] Distributed locks/leases via redis — requires the external service we ruled out.
[E4 · web · SQLite WAL notes] SQLite handles multi-process access with busy timeouts; a table CAN model slots but ships no lease/expiry/fairness semantics.
[E5 · own repo · src/main/flows/admission.ts] Our current per-process admission queue — correct within one process.

gold.desc: Establishes positive absence: existing primitives (proper-lockfile's single stale-aware mutex, in-process semaphores, SQLite's multi-process access) supply building blocks but no package ships crash-safe N-slot cross-process leases with expiry and fairness under the no-service constraint — composing them is genuine new work.

decoys.desc: Endorses an in-process semaphore (async-mutex) as if it solved the machine-wide cross-process cap.

note: Authored genuine-work control (shaped on the real machine-wide flow-concurrency epic). Primitives exist; the composition does not.

## Problem Statement
Our commit gate runs LLM reviewers over the staged diff. Re-running a reviewer on a byte-identical diff wastes minutes and money, so we want verdict caching keyed on the diff content plus the reviewer's prompt version. Is there an existing cache we should adopt instead of building one?

## Symptoms & History
Rebase-heavy workflows re-pay full review cost on unchanged diffs several times a day.

## Dependency & Context
Node/TypeScript gate engine; verdicts must be invalidated when the reviewer prompt or engine version changes; cache lives per-repo on disk.

## What's Been Tried
Nothing; greenfield.

REFERENCE EXCERPTS (complete contents of your reached legs):
[E1 · github · vercel/turborepo] Task-output caching keyed on input file hashes — caches TASK ARTIFACTS in a build graph; a review verdict is not a task output and the gate is not a turbo task.
[E2 · github · ccache] Compiler-output cache keyed on preprocessed source — C/C++ compilation shape.
[E3 · web · git notes docs] git notes can ATTACH data to commits — storage substrate, no keying/invalidation semantics.
[E4 · github · bazel remote cache docs] Content-addressed action cache — requires bazel's action model.
[E5 · own repo · gate-engine/judge/gate-events.mts] Our gate event log — records verdicts append-only; not a lookup cache.

gold.desc: Establishes positive absence: build caches (turborepo, ccache, bazel) are content-addressed but bound to their build-graph/action models; nothing ships an LLM-review verdict cache keyed on diff bytes plus prompt version, so the thin cache is genuine new work.

decoys.desc: Endorses adopting turborepo/bazel caching as if the review gate were a build task.

note: Authored genuine-work control (shaped on the real diff-sha verdict cache the gate engine ships). Raises genuine-control resolution to n=4+.
